findings.evidence: 6. **Choose the theme mechanism.** ... Reuse an established styling system; use Tailwind variants or a ThemeProvider only when the project already depends on it or needs runtime theme objects.
findings.fix: Keep the data-theme default but cut 'Reuse an established styling system...', which is generic advice. The model already avoids adding a second styling stack. Use the line for the non-obvious part instead, the pre-paint inline script from the Gotchas.

findings.evidence: Without one, do a keyboard-only pass and a 200%-zoom pass on the pilot screen in each theme and say so in the output.
findings.fix: Shorten this to a one-clause reminder, or name what typically breaks per theme (focus ring invisible on dark surfaces, hover role untested). Generic keyboard and zoom passes are activation-level content the model already knows.

findings.evidence: 5. **Derive the component hierarchy from use.** Levels: primitives, composed patterns ... Writing or reviewing component APIs in any framework: load `references/component-examples.md` ... Do NOT load the template for token-only work or a non-React stack.
findings.fix: Split step 5 into three short sub-bullets: (a) the promotion question 'do two consumers already use it with the same props?', (b) the prop rules (semantic props, slots, no root className/style), (c) the load triggers. Right now one dense paragraph mixes the thinking framework, the API rules and the routing, which weakens the Process pattern's checkpoints.

findings.evidence: Build the dialog primitive on native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a tested library, never `aria-modal` on a styled box.
findings.fix: Add the reason: 'because aria-modal only tells assistive tech the rest is inert; it does not trap focus, make the background inert or handle Escape and top-layer stacking, which showModal() does natively.'

findings.evidence: Should-trigger queries are terse and all name the domain ("Help me standardize colors and spacing across three product teams."). None tests the description's promise 'even when the user only says the screens look inconsistent or all over the place'. None has file paths or personal context.
findings.fix: Replace two or three terse positives with realistic indirect ones. Examples: "my PM says our admin app and the customer portal look like two different products, buttons and grays are all over the place - where do we even start?" and "we have src/styles/colors.css with 40 hex values copy-pasted around, can we clean this up so the mobile team can reuse it?"

Eval 'accessible-dark-tokens' lists the skill's own bundled resources as input files. Remove them (the prompt needs no input), or point at a real input under evals/files/, so the with-skill and without-skill runs get the same inputs. The casual-brand-kit expected_output ('A practical starter covering...') also needs a concrete statement of success.
